Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry.   I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.
papers.summary: The paper chronicles the rise and fall of BSM optimism from 1978 to 2000, focusing on naturalness, supersymmetry, and the eventual shift toward the string landscape and Split Supersymmetry. It highlights how experimental null results reshaped theoretical priorities and introduced the anthropic perspective on the cosmological constant.

papers.title: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics
papers.authors: Alan Chodos, Anastasiia Purtova
papers.abstract: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics. We also perform a perturbation analysis about an exact solution studied in earlier work. The equations represent a system that is subject to a periodic driver, and we use Floquet theory to help determine its properties. Numerically, we compare the exact solution to the analytic approximation, and we exhibit several examples of how the non-linear effects influence particle trajectories, with particular emphasis on trajectories near the linear limit.
papers.summary: This work studies a non‑linear modification of quantum mechanics, showing that in a particular limit the dynamics collapse to the standard linear theory and performing a perturbative Floquet analysis around a known exact solution. Numerical simulations illustrate how the non‑linear terms alter particle trajectories, especially near the linear regime.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
papers.authors: Akira Otsuki, Yuta Yamamoto, Kokin Cho, Rikuto Fushio, Masahito Yamazaki
papers.abstract: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $\chi$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $\chi$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.
papers.summary: This work analyzes how finite bond dimension truncation errors in LoopTNR of the six‑vertex model manifest as specific operators in the transfer‑matrix spectrum, identifying the dimerization operator as dominant under O(2) symmetry and quantifying its growth via conformal perturbation theory. The study shows that increasing bond dimension reduces initial error amplitudes but does not alter the operator hierarchy or growth rates across a range of Luttinger parameters.

papers.title: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
papers.authors: Laura Batini, Valerio Pagni, Nicol\`o Defenu
papers.abstract: Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size. For interactions decaying as $1/r^{1+\sigma}$, this surface cost instead depends on the droplet size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as $R_c\propto h^{-1/\sigma}$ at small $h$, where $h>0$ is the bias field. The value $\sigma=1$ separates two regimes: for $\sigma<1$, the activation barrier diverges as $h\to0^+$; at $\sigma=1$, it grows logarithmically; and for $\sigma>1$, it remains finite, as in the nearest-neighbor chain. A nonlocal $\phi^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.
papers.summary: This paper studies nucleation of critical droplets in one-dimensional Ising chains with long-range interactions decaying as 1/r^{1+σ}. It finds that the droplet radius and activation barrier scale with the bias field h in a way that depends on σ, and confirms these results with a nonlocal φ^4 field theory and stochastic dynamics.

papers.title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
papers.authors: F. A. Brito
papers.abstract: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a 7‑dimensional thick‑to‑thin brane junction that localizes a Majorana fermion as a dark‑matter candidate, with a real scalar mediator enabling s‑wave annihilation and a light chiral mode contributing to dark radiation. The authors compute the relic abundance and predict a small ΔNeff in the range 0.05–0.076 for DM masses 10 GeV–1.5 TeV, testable by upcoming CMB experiments.

papers.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
papers.authors: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber
papers.abstract: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.
papers.summary: This paper presents continuum‑extrapolated results for the equation of state of 2+1+1‑flavor QCD at the physical point using the complex Langevin method, computing thermodynamic observables such as baryon density, pressure, speed of sound, and compressibility at high baryon chemical potentials. The study extends lattice QCD simulations into the regime above the crossover temperature with unprecedentedly large chemical potentials, offering new insights into hot and dense QCD matter.

papers.title: Galaxy Bias and Soft Limits from Inflation
papers.authors: Charalampos Nikolis, Henrique Rubira
papers.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) leaves an imprint on large-scale structure through a scale-dependent galaxy bias, and properly incorporating the effects of higher order PNG into the bias expansion requires a consistent renormalization framework that extends beyond the squeezed limit of the bispectrum. We develop the multi-loop renormalization of bias operators in the presence of non-vanishing primordial n-point functions of arbitrary order, including stochastic contributions. We show that galaxy bias renormalization is determined by the multi-soft limits of primordial correlators and bias kernels. We provide explicit computations for one- and two-loop renormalization of deterministic operators up to fifth order in the bias expansion. Finally, we derive the renormalization group equations for the bias parameters at one and two loops.
papers.summary: This paper develops a systematic multi-loop renormalization framework for galaxy bias operators in the presence of arbitrary-order primordial n-point functions, extending beyond the squeezed bispectrum limit. It provides explicit one- and two-loop computations up to fifth order and derives renormalization group equations for bias parameters, offering a comprehensive treatment of higher-point primordial non-Gaussianity effects on large-scale structure.

papers.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
papers.authors: Glenn Barnich
papers.abstract: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.
papers.summary: This paper rewrites the fourth‑order parabolic evolution equation governing Robinson–Trautman spacetimes as an energy balance for an asymptotically timelike observer, interpreting the nonlinear memory term as heat. The resulting first law of non‑equilibrium thermodynamics yields a local temperature and a strictly increasing entropy density from the environment’s perspective.

papers.title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
papers.authors: Tokiro Numasawa, Boris De Vos, Masataka Watanabe, Atsushi Ueda
papers.abstract: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. Here, we propose an alternative accurate and fast algorithm, where we read off the CFT spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution. We apply this method to extract the charge-resolved spectrum of a Haagerup CFT to higher levels and obtain a central charge $c = 2.137(27)$. Moreover, we show that the Maldacena--Ludwig monopole boundary can be realized as the ground state of the Fidkowski--Kitaev Hamiltonian after space-time rotation.
papers.summary: The authors present a rapid algorithm to extract the full CFT spectrum from the transfer‑matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state, applying it to the Haagerup CFT and determining its central charge to high precision. They also show that the Maldacena–Ludwig monopole boundary can be engineered as the ground state of the Fidkowski–Kitaev Hamiltonian via a space–time rotation.

papers.title: Weyl-induced ultrasoft renormalization of the static QCD potential
papers.authors: Michael Wilson
papers.abstract:
We derive the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet potential in potential nonrelativistic QCD. In a Ricci-flat background the electric Weyl tensor introduces a $t^{-2}$ term in the short-time chromoelectric correlator. The resulting dipole self-energy is ultraviolet divergent at order $\alpha_s^2$ in the curvature sector, two orders earlier than the flat-space contribution. For $W=C_{\mu\alpha
u eta}r^\mu u^\alpha r^
u u^ eta$ and $V_s^{(W)}=c_W W/r$, we obtain $
u\,\partial_
u c_W=C_F C_A\alpha_s^2/(3\pi)$. We calculate the compensating soft infrared pole and the finite one-loop matching coefficient in an optical dimensional subtraction scheme. A direct physical-metric fermion calculation reproduces the finite light-flavor term. We also exhibit the cancellation of the leading regulated infrared overlap and the compensating transformation of soft and ultrasoft constants under an evanescent curvature rescaling. In the perturbative adiabatic regime the anomalous dimension fixes the coefficient of a curvature-dependent $\alpha_s^2\ln\alpha_s$ term in the static energy.
papers.summary: The paper computes the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet QCD potential in a Ricci-flat background, showing that the Weyl tensor induces a $t^{-2}$ term in the chromoelectric correlator and leads to a UV divergence at order $alpha_s^2$ in the curvature sector. Using dimensional subtraction, the authors determine the compensating soft infrared pole, the one-loop matching coefficient, and demonstrate the cancellation of regulated infrared overlap, thereby fixing a curvature-dependent $alpha_s^2lnalpha_s$ term in the static energy.

papers.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
papers.authors: Nina Elkina, Alexander Pukhov
papers.abstract: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a stochastic sampler that aggregates soft photons into a single positive recoil, preserving the no-emission probability and key loss moments of the QED kernel. It demonstrates finite-step cooling bias and mitigates it via state feedback, with tests on laser and ion-channel setups to validate directed radiation spectra.

papers.title: Half-strings across the deconfinement transition of a $U(1)$ quantum link model
papers.authors: Indrajit Sau, Arnab Sen, Debasish Banerjee
papers.abstract: The phenomenon of confinement is arguably the key feature of gauge theories regularly studied in high-energy and condensed matter physics. This causes hadrons to exist as stable particles in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as bound states of quarks (and gluons), and strings in pure gauge theories. The promise of realizing such strings in quantum simulator setups have fueled extensive studies of a plethora of simpler lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Quantum link models (QLMs) generalize Wilsonian LGTs and yield richer scenarios of confinement. For example, the string joining two static charges in the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ $U(1)$ QLM fractionalize, giving rise to confining phases that break the point group and internal symmetries spontaneously. It was further shown in PRL 130, 071901 (2023) that adding annealed $Q = \pm 2$ charges to this model qualitatively changes the confinement-deconfinement transition. In this paper, we examine the finite temperature phase transition both in the presence and the absence of annealed charges through detailed extraction of critical temperature, $T_c$ , and exponents. The (effective) string tension $\sigma$ at zero and finite- temperatures are compared between the theory with and without annealed charges. The quantity $T_c/\sqrt{\sigma}$ for the QLM with annealed charges is similar to the usual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, while the theory without the charges provides a new universal value.
papers.summary: This study investigates the finite-temperature confinement–deconfinement transition in a spin-½ U(1) quantum link model, both with and without annealed ±2 charges, extracting critical temperatures and scaling exponents. The authors compare the resulting string tensions, finding that the presence of annealed charges yields a universal ratio T_c/√σ similar to the Z₂ gauge theory, while the pure model exhibits a distinct universal value.

papers.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
papers.authors: Yu-Bo Zhao, Ji-Wei Li, Zhi-Wei Wang
papers.abstract: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three predict completion, PD gives the largest gravitational-wave peak amplitude, followed by Parwani and AE. The non-conformal model has no universal ordering, and the prescription changes the type of thermal history across extended regions of parameter space. For representative benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude and a factor of about fifty in peak frequency. In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. This intrinsic ambiguity is smaller than the largest differences between prescriptions. Thermal resummation is a major source of uncertainty in these phase-transition and gravitational-wave predictions.
papers.summary: This study quantifies how different thermal resummation prescriptions affect the strength of first‑order electroweak phase transitions and the resulting gravitational‑wave signals in both classically conformal and non‑conformal two‑Higgs‑doublet models. It finds that multi‑field partial dressing yields the strongest, most supercooled transitions and largest GW amplitudes, while the choice of prescription introduces large uncertainties, up to nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude.

papers.title: Bianchi cosmologies with four-dimensional groups of motion in New General Relativity
papers.authors: Manuel Hohmann, Paul Martin Kull, Margus Saal
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of the most general metric teleparallel spacetimes of Bianchi types II, III and IX, which admit a four-dimensional symmetry group, in the 1-parameter family of New General Relativity. We first show that in each of these classes the most general metric teleparallel geometry is described by four free functions of time, while another four functions of time describe the most general energy-momentum tensor compatible with the same symmetries. We then derive the field equations of New General Relativity for this class of geometries. Finally, we present some solutions to these field equations. Our results show that both solutions resembling features of the standard Friedmann-Lema\^itre-Robertson-Walker cosmology of General Relativity and deviations thereof exist.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes Bianchi II, III, and IX cosmologies within the framework of New General Relativity, deriving the most general metric teleparallel geometries and their field equations. It presents explicit solutions that both reproduce and deviate from standard Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker cosmology.

papers.title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
papers.authors: Adri\'an Casado-Turri\'on, Paulo B. Ferraz, Mindaugas Kar\v{c}iauskas, Jos\'e Jaime Terente D\'iaz
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.
papers.summary: This paper develops a relativistic kinetic theory for collisionless particles whose mass varies, using a tilted Sasaki metric to adapt phase‑space geometry to variable mass and deriving how the one‑particle distribution function transforms between arbitrary conformal frames. It shows that the distribution function can be chosen gauge‑ and frame‑invariant, and the generalized Liouville equation holds in each frame.

papers.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
papers.authors: Jahed Abedi, Niayesh Afshordi
papers.abstract: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $\kappa$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $\omega=m\Omega_{\rm H}-ij\kappa$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $\Omega_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $\kappa$. These local statements leave the QNM spectrum unchanged but matter for merger ringdowns, because a source falling through the horizon drives the exterior at the horizon frequencies. Each QNM then has a driven and a free part, and the free part takes over only once the driving decays faster than the mode. The fundamental mode separates from the driving early. The overtones stay driven until the source is hidden behind the potential barrier, so overtone amplitudes fitted near the signal peak are in general not those of free oscillations. In GW250114, a ringdown model of the fundamental mode plus the first horizon mode, $\omega=2\Omega_{\rm H}-i\kappa$, is preferred over the fundamental mode plus its first overtone, with Bayes factors between 2 and 30, for start times from $2M_f$ before to $8M_f$ after coalescence. The horizon-mode fit returns a remnant that is heavier and spins faster than the inspiral predicts, as expected from nonlinear backreaction: the horizon that emits the mode has not yet settled to its final mass and spin. Zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms reproduce both the preference and the shift, which are therefore features of general relativity.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the role of horizon regularity in defining black hole quasinormal modes, introducing a new class of horizon modes with frequencies ω=mΩ_H−ijκ that are excited by sources crossing the horizon. The authors apply this framework to GW250114, finding that a model including the fundamental QNM and the first horizon mode fits the data better than one with the first overtone, suggesting that horizon-driven dynamics can affect early ringdown amplitudes.

papers.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
papers.authors: Luisa Eck, Paul Fendley
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $\theta=\pi$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.
papers.summary: The paper studies the integrable antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin‑1 chain, showing its low‑energy excitations are deconfined domain walls and proposing a non‑relativistic integrable field theory that reproduces the same low‑energy limit. It constructs the two‑particle scattering matrix for this theory, highlighting a quadratic gap closure at criticality.
